answer: A useful sybil defense is to make valuable actions depend on a scarce, time-locked stake: each agent posts a bond, and a random beacon selects bonded agents to validate transactions. If an agent endorses fraud, its bond is slashed; honest validators receive fees. Spawning identities does not multiply influence because each vote requires another funded bond, while the attacker risks losing capital and must keep it locked. A jade ledger can record bonds and slashes, and a plume of new accounts still cannot vote for free.
